newsitem.title: USA: Commerce to issue revised U.S. trade data April 25.
newsitem.headline: Commerce to issue revised U.S. trade data April 25.

text.p: The Commerce Department said on Friday that it will issue a revised and corrected report on February and January trade at 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT) on April 25.

"The revised report will correct all data series affected by the January and February data for crude petroleum imports as originally reported on April 17," the department said in a statement. Commerce said on Thursday that reporting errors had led it to overstate the value of February crude petroleum imports by about $1.1 billion, leading it to gauge incorrectly the size of the monthly trade deficit on goods and services.
The correct total deficit figure for February was $10.4 billion instead of $11.59 billion, Commerce said late Thursday, several hours after it issued its initial estimate.

On Friday, Commerce said a detailed examination of crude petroleum import documents "revealed that some of the documents submitted for February were actually related to crude petroleum transactions occurring in 1996 and 1995."

It said the Customs Service, an arm of the Treasury Department, collects all import and export documents and passes them on to the Commerce Department's census bureau for translation into monthly trade statistics.
Commerce said efforts to improve efficiency inadvertently helped create the error.

It said recent efforts by its census bureau and the Customs Service to more accurately check oil imports "produced a surge of documents received along with the February documents that should have been submitted in earlier periods."

Commerce said "separating real changes in trade from sporadic shifts in patterns of document submission" was complicated because its census bureau processes about 3.5 million records a month on goods trade in order to arrive at the monthly trade balance.
It said that January crude petroleum imports were overstated by about $300 million as a result of the late reports in addition to the $1.1 billion February overstatement.

Commerce said that 1996 and 1995 trade statistics will be adjusted to reflect the correct crude petroleum import figures when the census bureau issues its annual revision of prior-year trade statistics in June.
